//: Single-page app fallback: anything that is not a real file is served
index.html so the client router can handle it. Without this, opening a
share link directly — /share/<id>/<token> — returns Vercel's own 404,
because that path exists only in React Router and not on disk.
Rewrites are applied after the filesystem is checked, so real assets still
win: favicon.ico, manifest.json and everything under /static are served as
themselves rather than swallowed by the catch-all.
There is deliberately no `headers` block for /static. An earlier version
set immutable cache-control there and every asset under that prefix started
returning 404 while the rest of the site was fine — the rule matched the
path and the request stopped there instead of falling through. CRA already
emits content-hashed filenames and Vercel already caches them, so the rule
was buying nothing and cost the whole bundle.
